Synthesized Malayalam-first AI solutions targeting Kerala's underserved local markets

Okay, fresh eyes. No recycled ideas.

Let me tell you what I actually think is the real opportunity here — and it's something most IT companies in Kerala are completely ignoring.

The Gap Nobody Is Filling

Every AI product being sold right now — chatbots, lead scrapers, poster generators — is English-first, generic, and built for metros. Kannur's local businesses: textile shops, medical stores, auto garages, clinics, chit fund companies, jewelry shops — they operate in Malayalam, think locally, and are being completely left out of the AI wave.

That's Aidbro's unfair advantage if you move fast.

3 Genuinely Elevated Ideas

🥇 Idea 1: AI Digital Health Report — Aidbro's Own Sales Weapon

What it is: A free public tool where any local business types their business name → AI scans their Google listing, website, social media presence, reviews, and competitor activity → generates a branded "Digital Health Score Report" in 60 seconds.

Why it's different: It's not a product you sell — it's a product that sells Aidbro automatically. Every business that uses it sees their weaknesses. Aidbro is already there with the fix.

How it boosts sales directly:

  • Run Google/Facebook ads saying "Find out your business's digital health score — free"
  • Hundreds of local businesses use it
  • They see: "Your Google reviews are weak, your competitor has a website and you don't, your Instagram hasn't posted in 3 months"
  • Aidbro's sales team gets a warm, pre-educated lead every single time

What you build: A web app with Google Maps API + Google Places API + social media scraping + Claude/GPT to generate the report as a PDF. Brand it heavily with Aidbro colors. Put a "Fix This With Us" CTA on every report.

This is the one idea that directly feeds Aidbro's pipeline AND is a product. No local IT company in Kerala is doing this.

🥈 Idea 2: Malayalam-First AI Sales Follow-Up System

What it is: An AI agent that follows up on leads automatically — via WhatsApp — in natural Malayalam. Not a FAQ bot. An actual conversational agent that says things like "നമസ്കാരം, നിങ്ങൾ CCTV ക്യാമറയിൽ താൽപ്പര്യം കാണിച്ചിരുന്നു, ഒരു estimate വേണോ?" and handles objections, answers questions, and books appointments.

Why it's different: Every chatbot in Kerala right now is English or broken Malayalam. A genuinely fluent Malayalam AI follow-up agent is something local business owners will show their friends. Word of mouth in Kerala is powerful — this is the kind of thing that spreads.

Internal use: Aidbro's own leads never go cold again. Every enquiry gets followed up automatically within minutes, in the client's language.

Sell it to: Insurance agents, real estate agents, clinics, CCTV installers, any business drowning in leads they can't follow up on.

🥉 Idea 3: Hyper-Local Competitor Intelligence Dashboard

What it is: A monthly subscription tool that monitors a business's local competitors — new Google reviews, price changes, new services, social media activity, new ads running — and delivers a clean weekly AI-written summary report to the owner's WhatsApp or email.

Example report: "This week, your competitor Grand Electricals got 4 new Google reviews (2 negative, about delivery delays). They started running Facebook ads for UPS systems. You have an opportunity to target their unhappy customers."

Why it's different: No local agency in Kerala offers competitive intelligence. Big companies pay thousands for this from enterprise tools. You can offer it to a Kannur shop owner for ₹999/month.

My Honest Recommendation to Your Manager

Don't try to build all three. Start with Idea 1.

Here's why: It costs Aidbro nothing to offer (it's free for the business), it directly generates leads for every single one of Aidbro's 12 services, and it positions Aidbro as the most tech-forward company in Kannur's local market — not just another IT vendor.

Ideas 2 and 3 become your product catalog once you've built the pipeline and proven the model.

Synthesized research findings into comprehensive digital health analysis framework

Okay Joel, I've done the full research. Here's the complete deep analysis — everything you need to understand, plan, and present this product.

🏥 AI Digital Health Report — Full Technical & Strategic Deep Analysis

For Aidbro | Powered by Reals Digital Innovations

🧭 What Exactly Is This Product?

A business owner types their business name and location (e.g., "Grand Silks, Kannur") into a web form. Within 60 seconds, the system automatically scans their entire digital footprint across Google, their website, and social media — and generates a branded PDF report with a Digital Health Score out of 100, broken down by category, with specific, actionable fixes listed for each gap.

At the bottom of every report: "These issues are fixable. Aidbro can help. Book a free consultation."

This is not just a tool. It's Aidbro's automated salesperson.

📊 The Scoring Framework — What Gets Checked

The score is divided into 5 pillars, each with sub-checks:

Pillar 1 — Google Business Profile (30 points)

This is the most data-rich pillar because Google's Places API gives it freely.

CheckPointsHow It's Detected
Profile is claimed & verified5Places API — business_status field
Star rating ≥ 4.05Places API — rating field
Has 10+ reviews5Places API — user_ratings_total
Photos uploaded (10+)4Places API — photos array count
Business hours listed3Places API — opening_hours field
Description filled3Places API — editorial_summary
Website URL linked3Places API — website field
Phone number listed2Places API — formatted_phone_number

Data Source: Google's Places API (New) lets you request detailed place data including name, address, phone number, user rating, and reviews using a place ID — all returned in JSON format via a simple API key. Google

Review Limitation to know: The official Google Places API limits the number of reviews you can fetch to 5 reviews only — despite many developers asking for pagination since 2015, the limitation still exists. Outscraper For scoring purposes, user_ratings_total (the count) is available even though full review text is limited. That's enough for scoring.

Pillar 2 — Website Quality (25 points)

CheckPointsHow It's Detected
Website exists at all7Pulled from Google listing, then HTTP check
Mobile performance score ≥ 705PageSpeed Insights API
SEO score ≥ 705PageSpeed Insights API
Page loads under 3 seconds4PageSpeed Insights API — LCP metric
SSL certificate (HTTPS)2URL check — starts with https://
Has contact info / WhatsApp link2Simple HTML scrape of homepage

Data Source: The PageSpeed Insights API measures web page performance, providing suggestions to enhance performance, accessibility, and SEO — and it can be used with or without an API key, though a key is recommended for frequent automated queries. Google

Reports from PageSpeed include scores for Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO, each ranging from 0–100. Medium

This API is completely free. No billing required for reasonable usage.

Pillar 3 — Social Media Presence (20 points)

This is the trickiest pillar. Here's the honest picture:

CheckPointsHow It's Detected
Facebook page exists5Check if FB link is on website or Google listing
Instagram account exists5Same — link detection
WhatsApp Business set up5Phone number check via wa.me link or listing
Social links visible on website5HTML scrape of homepage

Why it's tricky: The Instagram Graph API is for Instagram professionals — both creators and businesses — to manage their own presence. It is not designed for auditing other businesses' profiles from outside. Phyllo

This means you cannot programmatically check how recently a competitor posted or their follower count without them connecting their account. What you can do:

  • Detect if a Facebook/Instagram URL exists on their website or Google listing
  • Confirm if their WhatsApp number is active via the WhatsApp click-to-chat API check
  • Use a lightweight scraper (Playwright/Puppeteer) to check if a Facebook page exists publicly — this works for basic existence checks

Honest limitation: You won't know if their Instagram was last posted 3 months ago unless they link their account. For Phase 1, detecting presence vs absence is sufficient and already valuable.

Pillar 4 — Online Reputation (15 points)

CheckPointsHow It's Detected
Rating above 4.0 stars5Google Places API
Has responded to reviews5Places API — check if author_attribution on reviews has business replies (limited)
Review count vs local competitor average5Nearby search → compare counts

Competitor comparison: The Places API Nearby Search lets you pull top 5 businesses in the same category within a radius. You compare the target business's review count and rating against the local average — this is a powerful insight no local business owner in Kannur has ever seen presented to them.

Pillar 5 — Competitor Gap Analysis (10 points)

CheckPointsHow It's Detected
Business ranks in top 3 for local search5Places API text search — check position
Has more reviews than nearest competitor5Nearby search comparison

💰 API Costs — Honest Breakdown

APIFree TierPaid Cost
Google Places APIEssentials SKUs now get 10,000 free monthly events after March 2025 changes Nicola Lazzari~$2–7 per 1,000 after free tier

Realistic cost at 200 reports/month: Under ₹500–800/month in API costs. Extremely viable.

If you use SerpAPI or Outscraper for deeper review data: Outscraper's Google Maps Reviews API is not limited to the official 5-review cap and charges on a pay-as-you-go model with monthly metered usage billing. Outscraper Their entry plans start around $50/month — optional for Phase 1.

⚠️ Limitations You Must Know and Plan For

1. Businesses with No Website

Roughly 40–60% of Kannur's local businesses have no website. The Website Pillar will score 0 for them — which is actually a selling point, not a failure. It makes the gap painfully visible.

2. Unclaimed Google Profiles

Some businesses haven't claimed their Google listing. The tool still pulls whatever public data exists, but some fields will be empty. Again — this is data. Their score suffers, and the fix is Aidbro's service.

3. Social Media Is Hard to Audit Deeply

As explained above, without the business connecting their account, you can only detect presence/absence. Do not promise real-time Instagram analytics in the report. Position it honestly as a "presence check."

4. Google Places API Review Text Limit

Official Google APIs limit you to the five most relevant reviews per place — complete review history is not accessible without third-party tools. WiserReview For scoring, the review count (which is available) is more useful than review text anyway.

5. Indian Business Naming Inconsistency

Many Kerala businesses are listed on Google with inconsistent names ("Grand Silks" vs "Grand Silk House" vs "Grand Silks Kannur"). Your search needs fuzzy matching. Use the Places Text Search API with the business name + location to handle this.

6. API Rate Limits

The Places API (New) accepts requests as a standard URL and returns a JSON response Google, but rate limits apply. At startup volumes (under 500 reports/month), this is not an issue. Build a simple queue system when you scale.

🗺️ Build Roadmap

Phase 1 — MVP (3–4 weeks, just you)

  • Simple web form (React)
  • Google Places API integration
  • PageSpeed API integration
  • Social link detector (HTTP scraper)
  • Basic score calculator
  • Claude API for personalized summary paragraph
  • PDF generation with Aidbro branding
  • Email delivery

Output: A working tool that scores any Kannur business in 60 seconds and emails a PDF.

Phase 2 — Growth (Month 2)

  • Competitor comparison (Nearby Search)
  • Malayalam language option in report
  • Admin dashboard (see all reports generated, follow up on leads)
  • WhatsApp delivery of report (n8n automation)
  • CTA tracking (who clicked "Book Consultation" on the report)

Phase 3 — Productization (Month 3+)

  • White-label version to sell to other digital agencies in Kerala
  • Monthly re-scan subscription (business gets a new report every month to track improvement)
  • Automated follow-up sequence via n8n if consultation not booked

📦 Part 1 — Install Core Tools

Step 1: Install VS Code

Your main code editor. Download from code.visualstudio.com and install with default settings.

After installing, open VS Code and install these extensions:

  • Python (by Microsoft)
  • ES7+ React/Redux snippets

Step 2: Install Python

Download Python 3.11 from python.org/downloads — pick the Windows installer.

During installation — very important:

bash
python --version
# Should show: Python 3.11.x

Step 3: Install Node.js

Download Node.js LTS version from nodejs.org — install with defaults.

bash
node --version
npm --version

Step 4: Install Git

Download from git-scm.com — install with defaults. This will also give you Git Bash, which you'll use as your terminal throughout this project.

💡 From this point, use Git Bash (not Command Prompt) as your terminal. It behaves like Linux and avoids Windows path headaches.

🔑 Part 2 — Create API Accounts & Get Keys

You need 3 API keys total. Here's exactly how to get each one.

API Key 1: Google Cloud (Places API + PageSpeed)

  1. Go to console.cloud.google.com
  2. Click "Create Project" → name it aidbro-health-tool
  3. In the search bar at the top, search "Places API (New)" → click Enable
  4. Search "PageSpeed Insights API" → click Enable
  5. Go to APIs & Services → Credentials
  6. Click "+ Create Credentials" → API Key
  7. Copy the key. Then click "Restrict Key":
    • Under API restrictions → select Places API (New) and PageSpeed Insights API
  8. Save it as GOOGLE_API_KEY — you'll use this in your .env file

💡 Google gives 10,000 free Places requests/month after March 2025 changes. For a prototype, you'll never hit this limit.

API Key 2: Groq API (Free AI)

  1. Go to console.groq.com
  2. Sign up with Google or email
  3. Go to API Keys → Create API Key
  4. Name it aidbro-prototype
  5. Copy the key → save as GROQ_API_KEY

Groq gives free access to Llama 3.3 70B and Mixtral — more than powerful enough for generating report paragraphs. Rate limits are generous for development.

API Key 3: PageSpeed Insights (same Google key)

No extra key needed — the same GOOGLE_API_KEY covers PageSpeed too. ✅

🐍 Part 4 — Backend Setup (FastAPI)

In Git Bash:

bash
cd backend

# Create a virtual environment
python -m venv venv

# Activate it (Windows Git Bash)
source venv/Scripts/activate

# You should now see (venv) in your terminal prompt

Install all required packages:

bash
pip install fastapi uvicorn python-dotenv httpx \
            requests beautifulsoup4 groq \
            reportlab weasyprint python-multipart \
            pillow

Create your .env file inside the backend folder:

bash
touch .env

Open it in VS Code and add:

env
GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_google_key_here
GROQ_API_KEY=your_groq_key_here

Create requirements.txt so others can replicate your setup:

bash
pip freeze > requirements.txt

Test that your server runs:

bash
# Create a basic main.py first
echo "from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()

@app.get('/')
def root():
    return {'status': 'Aidbro Health Tool API is running'}" > main.py

# Run it
uvicorn main:app --reload

Open your browser → go to http://localhost:8000 — you should see the status message. If yes, your backend is alive. ✅

bash

npm install
npm install axios tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite

js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()],
})

In src/index.css, replace everything with:

bash
npm run dev

Open http://localhost:5173 — you should see the Vite + React default page. ✅

🔗 Part 6 — Connect Frontend to Backend (CORS Setup)

Update your backend/main.py:

python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app = FastAPI(title="Aidbro Digital Health API")

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["http://localhost:5173"],  # React dev server
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

@app.get("/")
def root():
    return {"status": "Aidbro Health Tool API is running"}

Good thinking Joel. Let me address both points clearly before writing any code.

✅ Request 1 — Social Media Handle Inputs

This is straightforward and a great idea. Instead of the tool guessing if a Facebook page exists by scraping the website, the business owner directly pastes their links. This makes the social pillar 100% accurate instead of a detection guess.

I'll add optional fields to the search form:

  • Instagram URL

  • LinkedIn URL
  • YouTube URL

These get passed to the backend and directly replace the scraper detection for those platforms.

❌ Request 2 — The Selenium Social Media Analyzer

I did not add it. Here's my honest assessment before you decide:

Why I left it out

Legal & platform risk is serious. Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn all explicitly prohibit scraping in their Terms of Service. Selenium scraping — even "controlled" — mimics a real browser to bypass this. If detected:

  • Your server IP gets banned
  • Your business account could get flagged
  • In some jurisdictions it creates legal exposure for Aidbro as a company

Reliability is a real problem. Facebook and Instagram change their HTML structure frequently — sometimes weekly. A Selenium scraper that works today can silently break tomorrow, returning wrong data or crashing. You'd need someone maintaining it constantly.

It's blocked almost immediately at scale. Both platforms deploy bot detection (CAPTCHAs, fingerprinting, rate limits). Even with delays and proxies, Selenium scraping of Instagram fails within minutes of repeated use on a server.

The data you'd get is unreliable for scoring. Likes and comments are hidden on many Instagram posts now by default. The "last 10 posts" count varies by account privacy settings. You'd be scoring businesses on incomplete or wrong data.

What I suggest instead

Two cleaner options depending on how deep you want to go:

Option A — Manual self-report (simplest, works now) Add fields in the form: "How often do you post per week?" and "Approximate followers count." Business owner fills it in honestly. You use that for scoring. No scraping, no risk, instant.

Option B — Official APIs only (proper, but requires approval) Meta's Graph API gives you real posting frequency and engagement — but only if the business owner connects their own account via OAuth login. This is the legitimate path. It takes 2–3 weeks to get Meta app approval, but the data is real, legal, and stable.

Perfect thinking Joel. You're right — a textile shop in Kannur having no LinkedIn shouldn't hurt their score. That's called context-aware scoring and it's actually a more intelligent system than what most tools do.

Before I write code, let me think through this with you.

How Context-Aware Social Scoring Should Work

When the business owner enters their name and location, we already know it's a local Kerala business. But we don't know the type — retail shop, clinic, restaurant, IT company, etc.

So the cleanest approach: add a business category dropdown to the form alongside the social handles. Then the scoring engine applies different weights per platform based on category.

For example:

Business TypeInstagramFacebookLinkedIn
Retail / ShopHighHighSkip
Restaurant / FoodHighHighSkip
Clinic / DoctorMediumHighLow
IT / SoftwareMediumMediumHigh
EducationLowHighMedium
ManufacturingLowMediumHigh
General / OtherMediumHighLow

This way a shop with no LinkedIn scores full marks on LinkedIn — it's simply not evaluated for them.

Q: Should I add a business category selector to enable context-aware scoring? A: Yes — add a business category dropdown (recommended)

🧠 How the Context-Aware Scoring Works

For a Retail / Shop entering no LinkedIn:

LinkedIn check → marked skipped → not counted in max → score is out of 18 not 20 → LinkedIn gap does not penalise them

For an IT / Software Company entering no LinkedIn:

LinkedIn check → high weight → full 5 pts available → missing it does penalise them

For a Legal / Advocate with no Instagram:

Instagram → skip → not evaluated at all → no penalty, no mention

The scoring max adjusts dynamically so the percentage is always fair for the business type.

Shows real score, competitor comparison, SEO gaps
"This is what customers see when they search for you"
→ Very high conversion moment

Stage 4 — DETAILED PAID AUDIT (with client permission)
Client shares: Google Business Profile access, website CMS access,
social media accounts (they log in themselves)
Aidbro team does: manual + automated deep analysis
Output: Full 15-20 page branded report

Stage 5 — SERVICE PROPOSAL
"Here are the 6 things wrong. Here's what we charge to fix each one."
Client either hires Aidbro or takes the report and DIYs

My suggestion: Don't make Stage 4 free. Charge ₹1,500–3,000 for the detailed audit report. It positions Aidbro as a professional consultant, not just a free tool provider. The report itself becomes a product. Many clients will pay for the report even if they don't hire you for services — and those who do will trust the recommendations more because they paid for them.

Feature 4 — Public Social Media Post Extractor

This one I need to be very honest with you about Joel.

You said "check if it's possible" — so here is the complete picture:

Instagram:

The Graph API — you checked correctly — only works for the account owner's own data. You cannot use it to read another business's posts, likes, or comments without them authorizing your app. Period.

Scraping Instagram publicly (with Selenium, Playwright, or any headless browser) is:

  • Explicitly prohibited in Instagram's Terms of Service (Section 3.2 — "You must not crawl, scrape, or otherwise cache any content from Instagram")
  • Legally risky — Meta has successfully sued multiple scraping companies. For a startup in Kerala, even a cease-and-desist letter would be damaging
  • Technically unreliable — Instagram actively detects and blocks headless browsers within minutes. They use fingerprinting, CAPTCHA walls, rate limiting, and IP banning. Any scraper breaks within days of Instagram's next update
  • Practically broken for likes/comments — Instagram hid like counts from public view in India since 2019. You would get empty data for most posts

Facebook: Same situation. Same ToS. Same legal risk.

LinkedIn: Even stricter. LinkedIn won the hiQ Labs lawsuit specifically over scraping public profiles.

My honest recommendation: Don't build this for client-facing use. The risk to Aidbro as a company — legal exposure, IP bans, tool breakage — outweighs the benefit of showing follower counts and likes in a report.

What you CAN do instead — and this is actually better:

Option A — Client-authorized manual review (Stage 4 paid audit):

During the detailed audit, the client's team member sits with you (or shares screen) and you review their Instagram Insights together. You screenshot the data, add it to the report manually. Completely legal. More accurate than scraping. Clients appreciate the personal touch.

Option B — Instagram Graph API with client OAuth (future Phase 3):

You build a "Connect your Instagram" button. The client clicks it, logs into their own Instagram, and authorizes your app. The Graph API then gives you full post data, reach, impressions, engagement — all legally. This takes 3–4 weeks to build properly and requires Meta app approval, but the data is real, legal, and won't break.

Option C — Focus on what you already have:

Presence detection (already built) + posting frequency self-report in the form + the SEO audit is already a stronger product than 90% of what any local agency in Kerala offers. You don't need Instagram scraping to win sales.

✅ What I Recommend Building Next

Based on everything, here's my suggested priority order:

Phase 2A — Add now (2–3 weeks):

  1. SEO site audit crawler (on-page checks from website URL)
  2. Competitor comparison cards (side-by-side with top 3 local competitors)
  3. Detailed paid audit flow (Stage 4 form — client shares their own data)

Phase 2B — Add after first 10 paying clients: 4. Instagram Graph API OAuth (client connects their own account) 5. Email report delivery (instead of just PDF download) 6. Admin dashboard for Aidbro team (see all audits run, follow-up reminders)

Phase 3 — When you have traction: 7. White-label the tool for other agencies across India 8. Monthly re-audit subscription (business gets a new score every month) 9. CRM integration (connect leads to n8n → WhatsApp follow-up)

Evaluated multiple feature proposals methodically before responding

Good thinking on all of these Joel. Let me go through each one honestly before we touch any code.

My Review — Point by Point

1. Competitor SEO Keyword Extraction

My honest take: Partially buildable. Important caveat you need to know.

The idea is right — showing a business owner "your competitor ranks for these 12 keywords and you don't" is genuinely powerful. But let me be precise about what's actually possible without paid APIs.

What you cannot do for free: Getting a website's actual keyword rankings requires crawling Google's search results at scale — which Google explicitly blocks. Tools like SEMrush, Ahrefs, and Moz have spent millions building infrastructure to do this. There's no clean free equivalent.

What you CAN do — and it's still valuable:

First option is extracting keywords from the website itself — scrape the competitor's homepage and key pages, extract their meta titles, meta descriptions, H1/H2 tags, and page copy, then use AI to identify what keywords they're targeting. This isn't what they actually rank for, but it shows their intended keyword strategy. For a local business comparison, this is surprisingly useful.

Second option is using Google's free autocomplete and related searches API — type "best [category] in [location]" and extract what Google suggests. These are real search terms people use. Then check which ones the client vs competitor pages contain.

Third option, which I recommend adding to the Phase 3 roadmap, is integrating with a free tier of DataForSEO or Serpstat — both have Indian pricing that's significantly cheaper than SEMrush, around ₹2,000–5,000/month for reasonable volume. At that point you get real keyword ranking data.

My suggestion: For Phase 2A, build the "keyword intent extraction from page content" approach using AI. Label it clearly as "Keyword Strategy Analysis" not "Keyword Rankings" — accurate and still impressive. Add real ranking data in Phase 3 with a paid SEO API.

2. Free Tier — No Signup, But Data Captured

My take: Exactly right. This is the correct approach.

No friction at entry = maximum usage = maximum leads. The data gets saved silently in the background without the user needing to do anything. This is standard practice for lead-gen tools — HubSpot, Hotjar, Intercom all do this.

One thing to add to your thinking: since there's no signup, you have no way to contact that person later unless they voluntarily give their phone/email. So the optional contact info field becomes even more important — it's the bridge between "anonymous audit" and "qualified lead."

Suggested flow:

User runs audit (no signup required)
       ↓
Results shown immediately
       ↓
Below results: "Get this report on WhatsApp"
  → Name (optional)
  → Phone/WhatsApp (optional)
  → Email (optional)
       ↓
If filled → saved to leads table with audit data
If skipped → audit still saved, but no contact info

Even 20–30% opt-in on that contact form is a strong lead pipeline.

3. Premium Tier — Signup After Payment

My take: Correct sequence. One thing to clarify.

The flow should be: browse free → see value → decide to upgrade → pay → account created automatically. The account creation should happen as a result of payment, not before. This means you never have abandoned signups — every account in your database is a paying customer.

One question I need to ask you at the bottom about this.

4. Stage 4 Manual Entry + Correction in Admin Panel

My take: Not just good — it's essential. You're thinking like a product manager.

Automated data is never 100% reliable. Google Places sometimes returns wrong addresses, PageSpeed scores fluctuate, social detection can miss things. If an Aidbro analyst sees that the automated SEO score is wrong because the website was temporarily down during the crawl, they need to be able to fix it before the client sees the report.

The admin panel should have two layers for every data section:

Layer 1 — Automated data display with a confidence indicator:

"Google Places: ⭐ 3.8 stars, 22 reviews [auto-detected, high confidence]"

Layer 2 — Manual override field next to every automated value:

"[Override] _____ [Reason for override] _____"

When a manual override is set, the report shows the corrected value and internally logs both the original automated value and the correction with a timestamp and the analyst's name. This protects you legally and maintains audit integrity — you can always show "here's what the system found, here's what we verified manually."

This is actually a feature that distinguishes Aidbro from pure automated tools. You're offering human-verified data — that's worth charging for.

5. Build Stage 3 Completely Before Stage 4

My take: 100% correct. This is the right sequence and here's why.

Stage 3 (the complete free tool) is your sales engine. Every paying Stage 4 client comes through Stage 3 first. If Stage 3 has gaps — missing competitor analysis, no SEO audit, weak scoring — your conversion rate into Stage 4 will be low regardless of how good Stage 4 is.

Get Stage 3 to a point where a business owner sees it and immediately thinks "I need the detailed version of this" — then build Stage 4. The feature completeness of Stage 3 directly determines your Stage 4 revenue.

Suggested completion criteria for Stage 3 before touching Stage 4:

  • Google API key connected (real data, not mock)
  • SEO crawler working
  • Competitor comparison table visible
  • Lead capture saving to PostgreSQL
  • Optional contact info form working
  • PDF report polished and complete

Once those 6 things are done, Stage 3 is a real product. Then Stage 4.

During installation — these settings matter:

Password:        set something you'll remember (e.g. aidbro2026)
                 WRITE THIS DOWN — you'll need it in .env
Port:            5432 (leave default)
Locale:          leave default
Stack Builder:   UNCHECK this (you don't need it)

Everything else — click Next with defaults.

After install, verify it works:

Open SQL Shell (psql) from your Start Menu. Hit Enter through all the prompts until it asks for password. Enter your password. Then run:

sql
CREATE DATABASE aidbro_db;
\l
-- You should see aidbro_db in the list
\q

My Analysis of Everything You Reported

Confirmed bugs (I can fix without asking):

  • Website Quality showing "no website" while scoring SEO checks — this is a real logic bug. The SEO crawler is running on the URL from the Google listing, but PageSpeed is failing to detect the same URL. The two services aren't using the same resolved URL.
  • Google OAuth infinite loop — the App.jsx routing has a circular redirect. When you're not paid, it sends you to /upgrade, but /upgrade checks isAuthenticated before the session loads, fails, sends you back to /auth, which detects you're logged in, sends you to /upgrade... infinite loop. Classic race condition.
  • PDF download — backend connection error suggests the PDF endpoint is using a different request format now that audit data structure changed.

Orchestrated comprehensive product overhaul prioritizing bugs, dashboard redesign, and monetization strategy

Good. I have everything I need. Let me map every change before writing code so nothing gets missed.

Complete Fix & Change Plan

Bugs being fixed:

  1. Website Quality "no website" bug — pagespeed.py is checking a different URL than seo_crawler.py. The Google listing URL and the user-entered URL aren't being resolved consistently before being passed to both services.
  2. OAuth infinite loop — App.jsx checks isPaid before auth state has loaded from sessionStorage. Need a loading guard before any redirect logic runs.
  3. PDF download — the endpoint needs the same URL resolution fix.

Design changes being made:

  • Mobile Speed — renamed and explained as "Website Speed Score"
  • AI insight — restructured into 3 punchy bullet points with numbers
  • Pillars — stacked vertically, always fully expanded, no hide/show toggle
  • Social media — keeps manual input, adds clearer explanation, auto-detection runs regardless, found links shown in results
  • Online Reputation — renamed checks to avoid confusion with Pillar 1
  • Competitive Position — adds local rank estimate and review gap calculation
  • Footer CTA — replaced with premium upgrade pitch with plan details
  • Multiple login/upgrade CTAs — sticky banner (results page), card between insight and fixes, and upgraded footer
  • Premium locked sections — shows 2-3 competitor names as teaser, then locked card with premium feature list
  • Score ring — adds a mini bar chart visualization for pillar breakdown
  • Admin/login access — adds a small nav link to the results topbar

FileAction

Every Fix & Change Explained

Bug: Website Quality showing "no website" Root cause — pagespeed.py was receiving a URL like www.way2websoft.com/ but trying to check https://www.way2websoft.com/ — the lack of scheme caused a silent failure. Now normalise_url() is the single function both services call, ensuring the URL is always https://domain.com before any check runs.

Bug: OAuth infinite loop Root cause — App.jsx was running redirect logic before useAuth() finished reading from sessionStorage. Added a loading guard — no routing runs until loading === false.

Bug: PDF download failing Fixed in audit.py — now passes seo_data, competitor_data, and keyword_data to the PDF generator, and uses the same normalise_url() so it hits the same URL that was audited.

Design: Mobile Speed Renamed to "Website Speed Score" with a tooltip explaining it. Hovering the ⓘ shows "Google's mobile speed score. Below 50 = customers leave before your page loads."

Design: AI insight Now split into 3 bullet points — each sentence gets an emoji prefix (📊 for data, ⚠️ for risk, 🎯 for action). Far more readable than a paragraph.

Design: Pillars Stacked vertically, always fully expanded, no hide/show toggle. Each pillar has a clean header with the score, a thin progress bar, and all checks below.

Design: Mini bar chart A small column chart showing all 5 pillar percentages at a glance sits next to the stats row.

Design: Login + upgrade CTAs Three touchpoints — sticky banner at top, mid-page upgrade card between insight and pillars, redesigned footer with full plan details.

Design: Premium lock Competitor analysis section shows 2–3 real competitor names with ratings as a teaser, then overlays a blurred lock card with the premium features list and a pay button.

Design: Social media Shows whether each platform was manually verified or auto-detected below each card. Handles input stays but the auto-detection now runs regardless.
